title: bee gate says so when the durable stamp could not be reached
action: R4 of the plan. In run_gate_body (verbs/state_group/set_gate.rs:616-806) the block at :779-798 that stamps the workflow record's own gates.<name>.approved is guarded by `if let Some(wf) = ... find_live_workflow(...)`. When the feature's workflow record is already status=closed that block is SILENTLY SKIPPED — no error, no warning — and the command still prints its ordinary success line (:800-804). Meanwhile write_through_projection has already written approved_gates.<name> into the lane record through its direct-write branch. The result is a half-write reported as a whole one, and it is what hid the stranded-approval defect through three merges before anyone noticed. FIX: when the durable stamp is skipped because no live workflow names the target feature, emit ONE additional line beside the success line, naming what happened in the operator's own terms — the approval was recorded on the lane record, the feature's workflow record is closed so the durable copy could not be updated, and (for uat specifically) the door reads the lane record as its second source. Keep the existing success line byte-identical: this is an added line, never a replacement, and never a refusal — the lane write is real and, once uad-1 lands, reachable. Add the same fact to the JSON result as a typed field rather than only as prose, so a non-interactive caller can see it too. This cell does NOT change which record is written, does not reopen anything, and does not touch the gate's approval semantics.

truths: Approving a gate on a feature whose workflow record is closed emits the warning line and carries the same fact as a typed field in the JSON result.
Approving a gate on a feature with a live workflow record emits no such line and no such field.
The existing success line is byte-identical in both cases — the warning is added beside it, never in place of it.
The command still exits 0 in both cases; nothing about this cell refuses.
Which record gets written is unchanged, and no closed record is reopened.

done_when: A gate approval that cannot reach the durable record says so, in both the text and the JSON, while the success line and the write itself are untouched.
notes: Phase 2 of the plan. Disjoint from uad-1, which touches uat.rs, verbs/worktree/ and verbs/drivers/close.rs. Do not edit those here. Runs in parallel with uad-1.
